briefs.title: Grok Bot 1.0 ships with Team Bots, meeting joins, and Mac local access; 4.8 soft rollout still pending confirmation
points: SpaceXSI (Nov 11): Introduced Grok Bot 1.0. Bots can be shared (Team Bots) and are more collaborative. Features include joining Google Meet/Zoom/Teams calls (answer in chat, send summaries), more proactive behavior, better self-improvement/memory of team workflows, and significantly improved browser use.

Grok Bot on Mac (Nov 12–13): Can now access Messages, Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Location, and Contacts. Musk highlighted real-world use (Maye Musk: Bot moved 2000 Dropbox photos in 5 minutes after offering to do it).

Alex Finn (practitioner, Nov 11–13): Called 1.0 massive (prior was beta); listed multiplayer Team Bots, call joining/action, proactivity, better browser. Separate post: download Bot and have autonomous revenue army by night; his made $1,800. Zero programming required.

Musk (Nov 10): Pre-training done for Grok 4.8; now in RL with evals climbing. Soft rollout to Bot users later that week. Entire stack rewritten from JAX/SGLang to C/C++. 'Will bear no resemblance to 4.7.' Foundations right; not yet incredible. As of Nov 13, no confirmed public live status or independent AA score.

AA Intelligence Index v5 (latest): Fable 5.2 ~64.6 (leader, $8/$40), Gemini 4 Carbon 60 ($2/$10 intro), Opus 5.5 ~59.1 ($4/$20), Astra ~56.9 ($10/$50), Sol ~54.6 ($2/$10), Grok 4.7 ~35.5 ($2/$6). No change in Grok ranking.
briefs.assumption: Grok 4.8 soft Bot rollout was planned for the week of Nov 10 but remains unconfirmed as live with no public AA scores or API identifier. Bot 1.0 usage economics and weekly limits still under prior cost pressure. Team Bot and meeting features depend on plan tier.

briefs.title: Grok 4.8 soft Bot rollout this week after C/C++ stack rewrite; Fable 5.2 leads AA Index
points: Musk (Nov 10): Pre-training finished for Grok 4.8; model now in RL with evals climbing. Soft rollout to Grok Bot users later this week. Entire RL and inference stack rewritten from JAX/SGLang into C/C++ (derived from Starlink engineering). 'Will bear no resemblance to 4.7 (thankfully).' Foundations built right; expects it to evolve into something special. Not yet incredible.
Musk: Opus 5.5 is a masterpiece; Grok 5 should exceed it in 2–3 months with continued acceleration.
Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic, ~Nov 9): tops AA Intelligence Index v5 at ~64.6 (max). Gemini 4 Carbon ~60, Opus 5.5 ~59.1, GPT-6 Astra ~56.9. Grok 4.7 remains ~35.5. Pricing: Fable $8/$40.
Alex Finn (Nov 11): Shares prompt for Grok Bot (or similar agents) to propose systems, subagents, and routines that reduce cognitive load based on shared history.
Alex Finn on Fable 5.2: Use for thorough planning and task creation, then hand execution to Opus 5.5 and testing to Sonnet/Haiku for better results and lower token use.
briefs.assumption: Soft rollout limited to Bot users; full API and independent AA scores for 4.8 unknown. Stack rewrite targets serving cost and reliability. Grok 5 timeline remains Musk's projection.

briefs.title: Musk reviews Grok Bot team for overnight fixes; practitioners detail full autonomous workflows
points: Musk (Nov 9): conducted round-table with Grok Bot engineering team; fixes implemented overnight with expectation of dramatic improvement by next day. Invites remaining issues via reply.

Alex Finn (Nov 7, practitioner): after months of heavy use, calls Grok Bot the best AI agent due to UX; lists concrete automations including 15-min X monitoring of AI accounts, fully autonomous revenue-generating business, continuous app testing + PR generation, content repurposing, 24/7 community monitoring/DMs, and retention outreach from product analytics.
Grok app growth (Oct): ~93.4M monthly active users, 12.7M downloads (per Musk RT of metrics).

AA Intelligence Index v5 (latest independent): Grok 4.7 ~35 (notable drop vs prior private-test readings); usable leaders Claude Opus 5.5 ~59, GPT-6 Astra ~57, GPT-6.1 Sol / Sonnet 5.5 ~55. Gemini 4 Carbon 60 remains limited-access. Pricing unchanged across flagships.
API watermark for grok-4.7 and related models live since Nov 7 (invisible statistical; team opt-out available).
briefs.assumption: Overnight fixes address reported reliability/UX friction; exact nature of improvements not detailed. Grok 4.8 release date remains unconfirmed. Bot unit economics still under pressure from always-on usage.

briefs.title: Grok Bot serving costs force tighter usage limits; practitioners publish workarounds
points: Musk confirmed Nov 1 that Grok Bot serving costs were unsustainably high relative to revenue; weekly allowances were reduced (users reported hitting 100% early over the Halloween weekend).
No public numbers on the new caps; Musk pointed users toward higher-tier plans for more usage.
Alex Finn (practitioner): Grok Bot is currently the best AI agent; published a video with 7 techniques to stretch token usage substantially (Nov 5).
Product continues shipping: Bot can place phone calls (dentist insurance check example); Grok Build multi-agent reliability upgrades; daily fixes noted by Musk.
AA Intelligence Index v5 (latest readings): Gemini 4 Carbon 60 (limited), Claude Opus 5.5 ~59, GPT-6 Astra ~57, GPT-6.1 Sol 55, Claude Sonnet 5.5 ~55, Grok 4.7 ~35. Pricing unchanged.
API text watermark for grok-4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5 / 4.3 and selected 4.20 variants goes live Nov 7.
briefs.assumption: Exact new weekly allowance figures not published; unit economics of always-on agents remain under pressure until cheaper inference or pricing adjustments. Grok 4.8 still has no firm public date.

briefs.title: Grok API text watermark starts Nov 7; Bot Pages continue to mature
points: SpaceXSI docs: from Nov 7, text from grok-4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5 / 4.3 and selected 4.20 variants will include an invisible statistical watermark by default (Responses and Chat Completions). Team admins can opt out per model; opt-outs audit-logged.
Grok Bot Pages & dashboards (shipped ~Oct 29) seeing practitioner adoption; Alex Finn highlights router/worker + attention-protection patterns that already match Grok Bot’s chief-of-staff design.
Musk continues RTing strong Grok Bot user feedback and notes daily fixes/features.

AA Intelligence Index v5 (private-test heavy) still ranks Grok 4.7 ~35 vs Gemini 4 Carbon 59, Claude Opus 5.5 58, GPT-6 Astra 57. Pricing unchanged: Grok $2/$6, Opus $4/$20, Astra $10/$50, Sol $2/$10.
briefs.assumption: Watermark is statistical/invisible and does not alter model behavior; exact opt-out scope and downstream redistribution impact still to be observed. Grok 4.8 timeline remains unconfirmed.

briefs.title: Musk: Grok 4.8 delayed but will be useful; not optimizing for benchmarks
points: Musk posts that Grok 4.8 has taken longer than expected but “will not be a disappointment.”
Explicitly states not optimizing for benchmarks; prioritizes usefulness.
Earlier (Sep 14): 2.5T model trained on new C++ stack finishing pretrain then RL; 4.8 noticeable improvement, 4.9 probably Astra/Fable class, Grok 5 maybe better than anything.
AA Intelligence Index v5 (Oct 27) ranks Grok 4.7 ~35; leaders Claude Opus 5.5 ~58, GPT-6 Astra ~57, Gemini 4 Carbon 59 (limited).
briefs.assumption: Grok 4.8 public release still weeks away; exact AA recovery unknown until independent measurement.

briefs.title: Grok Bot ships pages and dashboards
points: Alex Finn (practitioner) calls it the biggest Grok Bot update yet.
Pages and dashboards address prior usability limits; video demos multiple dashboards including one that reduces usage.
Bot continues to run on its own cloud computer with connectors and app access.

briefs.title: Grok Voice 3.0 launches at $0.08/min
points: Speech-to-speech model with sub-second latency.
Same price as Voice 2.0; available in Voice Agent API and Builder.
SpaceX reports 70% of Starlink support calls resolved autonomously.
Powers voice mode in Grok Bot and Tesla.

briefs.title: Grok 4.7 ships as current flagship
points: Released Sep 21; available in API (grok-4.7), Cursor, Grok Build, Bedrock, Foundry.
Pricing held at $2 input / $6 output per M (cached $0.5); 500k context.
Reasoning effort low/medium/high/xhigh; positioned for coding, agents, knowledge work.
Lab claims improvements on CursorBench, DeepSWE, verification, longer tasks.
